_comment: ADR-014: images are cosign-signed in CI and clients enforce the signature.
This is one half of the client side. The other half is
registries.d/meridian.yaml — WITHOUT IT THIS RULE REJECTS EVERYTHING,
because containers-image never fetches the signature to check.
ADR-023: the trust anchor must be RECOVERABLE, so this trusts a SET of
keys, not one. A fleet that enforces exactly one key is unrecoverable if
that key is lost or leaked: you cannot sign the image that would introduce
its replacement. For an auto-updating OS that is a permanent fleet-wide loss
of the update path — worse than a bad update, which rolls back.
`keyPaths` (plural) is the mechanism. NOTE FOR ANYONE EDITING THIS: two
sigstoreSigned requirements side by side in this array would NOT mean 'either
key'. Multiple requirements in a scope are ANDed — verified empirically —
so that shape demands BOTH signatures and breaks the rotation overlap
instead of providing it.
INCOMPLETE: the recovery key is not here yet. Its private half must be
generated offline and kept in cold storage, never in CI or any secret
store, so only the owner can produce it. ADR-023 makes adding it a
WP-04 deliverable that GATES THE FIRST :stable IMAGE. Until then this
fleet has one key and is not recoverable.
THE DEFAULT IS PERMISSIVE AND THAT IS A DEVELOPMENT STATE (ADR-022):
:testing-only, until the key exists, CI signs with it, and the NEGATIVE
TEST demonstrates that an unsigned image is REFUSED on a real machine.
